answer: Random Nectar Assignment. Each round, a verifiable random function keyed to a public seed assigns every registered agent a nectar allotment of task slots; the seed is revealed only at round start, so attackers cannot precompute which identities will receive work. Identities that fail a quill challenge—signing a fresh random nonce within the round—forfeit their allotment. An attacker must maintain each fake identity through repeated unpredictable rounds, paying real compute and hosting per identity, with no guarantee of yield until the ember of the seed is disclosed.
